newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Ex-Im Bank says no change on Three Gorges.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Ex-Im Bank says no change on Three Gorges.

text.p: The U.S. Export-Import Bank made clear on Wednesday it had no plans to review its decision to withhold export financing for the massive Three Gorges dam project in China, until the Chinese government provided information that the bank had requested.

The comment came in response to a July 24 Reuters report, from an interview with an Ex-Im official in Shanghai, that the bank hoped to reassess the controversial hydroelectric project to try to help U.S. exporters win contracts to build the dam.
An Ex-Im Bank spokesman in Washington said the remarks by the bank's business development officer in Shanghai, Annmarie Emmet, had been misinterpreted.
"Where we are is where we have been for over a year," said spokesman David Carter.
"We have been awaiting information from the Chinese government. We've received no information that would cause us to reconsider," he said.
The bank has asked for information on the environmental impact of the world's biggest water control project, including the impact of flooding areas that now have landfills.
Emmet had said she was "very hopeful Ex-Im Bank can get the material that it needs in order to assist in future contracts where we can contribute."
Under a 1992 U.S. law, the Ex-Im Bank must take environmental factors into account when assessing whether to support exports for a foreign project.
Three Gorges, which would dam China's Yangtze River, has come under heavy criticism from green groups.

China is reviewing tenders from several consortiums, with few U.S. companies participating, to supply the first group of generating units for the project and is due to announce the winners this month.
